correctness.rationale: For both explicit connected seven-vertex motifs, polynomial eigenvectors satisfy the exact adjacency eigenvalue equation modulo irreducible p2 or p3, and their binary bridge selectors are orthogonal at every root, yielding compact cell-supported eigenfunctions on the connected periodic graphs. The five roots are real and distinct by discriminants 17 and 316 and coprimality. Complete enumeration of 156 finite simple six-vertex graph isomorphism classes includes disconnected cases; no characteristic polynomial is divisible by either minimal polynomial. A six-cell compactly supported eigenfunction would require such divisibility, so no six-cell realization is possible. All identities are exact symbolic, and the finite graph enumeration is genuinely exhaustive of the finite input domain.

originality.rationale: The 2023 source poses the odd-even equality after explicit calculations only through five cell vertices; its selector sufficiency criterion alone does not imply the five seven-cell constructions are absent at size six. The 156-graph exact census gives the missing minimality and refutes the proposed equality. Targeted published-finding corpus searches for source ID, exact polynomials, selectors, seven-versus-six cells, and aliases found no implication-equivalent record; the 2025 genericity theorems do not give or imply this precise unweighted spectral-set separation. A targeted exact-polynomial web search recovered both factors from the 24-vertex McGee graph spectrum; this is not an implication-equivalent seven-cell periodic selector construction or six-cell obstruction.
residual_risks: A weakly indexed preprint or graph-spectrum catalogue could contain the same five seven-versus-six separating values without using single-cell flat-band terminology.
The finite atlas is exhaustive for simple unweighted motifs only, not weighted or potential-bearing operators.
The finding concerns a strict inclusion of at least five energies, not a complete description of the seven-cell spectral set.

The quadratic and cubic energy values are not new as abstract finite-graph eigenvalues: both occur in the McGee graph spectrum. The originality claim is restricted to their seven-cell periodic realization and six-cell obstruction.
